verdict: Leads dropped sharply this week; Google spend is not converting.
narrative: In the last 28 days, you received 26 leads at an average cost of $145.31 per lead — and this week that cost nearly doubled compared to the prior week as lead volume fell by 54%. Meta carried all 26 of those leads while Google Ads spent $2,564.83 and returned only 5 conversions, a clear efficiency problem that is being addressed by rebalancing how budget is allocated across channels. Separately, your intake pipeline shows 119 open opportunities but zero converted and zero appointments booked, which points to a follow-up gap that sits outside of advertising. We're working to close both issues in parallel, and local search visibility — which also dipped this week — is being monitored as a contributing factor to top-of-funnel pressure.

watch_item.issue: Google Ads is spending the majority of the paid budget — $2,564.83 this period — while producing only 5 conversions, nearly doubling your blended cost per lead week-over-week.
watch_item.fix: Budget allocation is being shifted toward Meta where leads are actually coming in, and Google campaign structure is under active review to improve conversion efficiency.
